title: Part
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. On the first face, draw a two-dimensional sketch consisting of a rectangular loop. The first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.0188, 0.0). The second line extends from (0.0188, 0.0) to (0.0188, 0.0188). The third line runs from (0.0188, 0.0188) to (0.0, 0.0188), and the fourth line completes the rectangle by going from (0.0, 0.0188) back to the origin. Apply a scale factor of 0.0188 to the entire sketch to adjust its size. Since the coordinate system is already aligned with the origin and has no rotation, no further transformation is necessary. Extrude the scaled sketch 0.75 units along the normal direction without extending it in the opposite direction. This extrusion forms a new solid body. The final dimensions of the part are a length of 0.01875 units, a width of 0.01875 units, and a height of 0.75 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.box(0.0188, 0.0188, 0.75, centered=(False, False, False))

# The box command creates a box with the specified dimensions
# The centered parameter is set to False to start the box from the origin (0, 0, 0)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Define the dimensions
length = 0.7500
width = 0.0188
height = 0.0188

# Define the sketch for the body
r = cq.Workplane("XY") \
    .moveTo(0, 0.002) \
    .lineTo(0, 0.0168) \
    .threePointArc((0.002, 0.0188), (0.002, 0.0168)) \
    .lineTo(0.0168, 0.0188) \
    .threePointArc((0.0188, 0.0168), (0.0168, 0.0168)) \
    .lineTo(0.0188, 0.002) \
    .threePointArc((0.0168, 0.0), (0.0168, 0.002)) \
    .lineTo(0.002, 0.0) \
    .threePointArc((0.0, 0.002), (0.0, 0.002)) \
    .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create the body
r = r.extrude(length)
